subject: Quantitative Aptitude
topic: Speed, Distance and Time — Trains and Relative Motion (W9)

questions.stem: A train travels 300 km in 5 hours. What is its speed in km/h?
questions.explanation: C is correct. Speed = Distance/Time = 300/5 = 60 km/h.
B is correct. Multiply by 5/18: 72×5/18 = 20 m/s. Short Trick: to convert km/h to m/s, multiply by 5/18. To go the other way, multiply by 18/5.

questions.stem: Ramesh walks at 5 km/h and reaches his office 10 minutes late. If he walks at 6 km/h, he reaches 10 minutes early. What is the distance to his office?
questions.explanation: C is correct. Difference in time = 20 min = 1/3 hour. d/5 − d/6 = 1/3 → d/30 = 1/3 → d = 10 km. Short Trick: distance = product of speeds × time difference / difference of speeds = (5×6×(20/60)) / (6−5) = 30×(1/3)/1 = 10.

questions.stem: Two trains of length 100 m and 150 m approach each other at 60 km/h and 90 km/h. How many seconds do they take to cross each other?
questions.explanation: C is correct. Relative speed (opposing) = 60+90 = 150 km/h = 150×5/18 = 125/3 m/s. Total length = 250 m. Time = 250 ÷ (125/3) = 250×3/125 = 6 s.

questions.stem: A person covers 60 km at 30 km/h and another 60 km at 60 km/h. What is his average speed for the entire journey?
questions.explanation: A is correct. Time for first 60 km = 2 h. Time for second 60 km = 1 h. Total = 120 km in 3 h. Avg = 40 km/h. Short Trick: same distance → avg = 2ab/(a+b) = 2×30×60/90 = 40 km/h. Never average the speeds directly.

questions.stem: A train passes a pole in 12 seconds and a 200 m platform in 20 seconds. Find the length of the train.
questions.explanation: C is correct. Speed is same in both cases. L/12 = (L+200)/20 → 20L = 12L+2400 → 8L = 2400 → L = 300 m. Speed = 300/12 = 25 m/s.

questions.stem: A person covers 40 km at 20 km/h and 60 km at 30 km/h. What is his average speed over the entire journey?
questions.explanation: C is correct. Time = 40/20 + 60/30 = 2+2 = 4 hours. Total distance = 100 km. Avg speed = 100/4 = 25 km/h. Note: averaging 20 and 30 gives 25 here coincidentally, but that only happens when times are equal, not distances.

questions.stem: Two cars start simultaneously from cities A and B, 120 km apart, and move towards each other at 40 km/h and 60 km/h respectively. After how many hours do they meet?
questions.explanation: C is correct. Relative speed = 40+60 = 100 km/h. Time = 120/100 = 1.2 hours. At meeting point, car A has covered 40×1.2 = 48 km from A.

questions.stem: A 200 m train travelling at 90 km/h overtakes another 300 m train travelling in the same direction at 36 km/h. How long does the overtaking take?
questions.explanation: D is correct. Relative speed (same direction) = 90−36 = 54 km/h = 54×5/18 = 15 m/s. Total length to clear = 200+300 = 500 m. Time = 500/15 = 100/3 = 33⅓ seconds.

questions.stem: A thief runs at 10 km/h. A policeman chases him from the same point 5 minutes later at 15 km/h. In how many minutes after the thief started running does the policeman catch him?
questions.explanation: C is correct. In 5 minutes, thief covers 10×5/60 = 5/6 km head start. Relative speed of policeman = 15−10 = 5 km/h. Time for policeman to close 5/6 km = (5/6)/5 = 1/6 hour = 10 minutes. Policeman started 5 minutes after thief → thief's total time = 5+10 = 15 minutes after he started.
